input.reasoning:
Estimation approach: converted story points to engineering hours using a baseline of ~6 hours/point for backend-heavy or migration work and ~5 hours/point for frontend/design work, then split hours across roles based on task nature (backend, frontend, QA, devops). Applied role capacity constraints (1.5 FTE Backend = ~120 hrs/wk, 1.0 FTE Frontend = ~40 hrs/wk equiv per person, 0.6 FTE QA = ~24 hrs/wk, 0.4 FTE DevOps = ~16 hrs/wk) to sanity-check that allocated hours are plausible for a multi-week delivery (assumed ~10-12 week project window). QA effort estimated at ~15-20% of dev hours per task depending on complexity/priority. DevOps effort concentrated on CI/pipeline setup (PW-1) and light involvement in migration (PW-8) and payment integration (PW-7) for infra/webhook deployment support. Non-labour costs added for Stripe sandbox/production fees, cloud staging environment, and a data migration tooling/Oracle export license allowance. A 12% contingency scenario and a 20% stretch scenario are provided for risk (P50/P70/P90 style) given no historical actuals exist for this client/team combo.

Task-level hour breakdown (approx):
PW-1 CI/staging (5 pts, High): Backend 16h, DevOps 40h, QA 8h
PW-2 Design system (8 pts, Medium): Frontend 90h, QA 12h
PW-3 Registration/login (8 pts, Urgent): Backend 60h, Frontend 30h, QA 20h
PW-4 RBAC (13 pts, High): Backend 90h, Frontend 30h, QA 24h
PW-5 Dashboard (8 pts, High): Backend 30h, Frontend 60h, QA 16h
PW-6 Invoice list/detail (5 pts, Medium): Backend 30h, Frontend 40h, QA 12h
PW-7 Payment integration (13 pts, Urgent): Backend 110h, Frontend 20h, QA 30h, DevOps 16h
PW-8 Legacy migration (21 pts, High): Backend 160h, QA 30h, DevOps 24h

Role totals:
Backend: 16+60+90+30+30+110+160 = 496h
Frontend: 90+30+30+60+40+20 = 270h
QA: 8+12+20+24+16+12+30+30 = 152h
DevOps: 40+16+24 = 80h

Capacity check over an assumed ~14-week (560 person-hours per 1.0 FTE at 40h/wk) delivery window:
Backend 1.5 FTE -> 1.5*40*14=840h capacity vs 496h needed: feasible.
Frontend 1.0 FTE -> 40*14=560h vs 270h needed: feasible, has slack for design system heavy load.
QA 0.6 FTE -> 24*14=336h vs 152h needed: feasible.
DevOps 0.4 FTE -> 16*14=224h vs 80h needed: feasible, though DevOps is thin and concentrated early (PW-1) which could bottleneck the start of the project since only 0.4 FTE is available for the critical-path CI/staging setup.

Priority totals computed by summing labour cost per task grouped by priority using role rates.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox + production setup fees and initial transaction testing
Staging/CI cloud environment costs (compute, storage) for pipeline duration
Data migration tooling / Oracle export utilities and temporary storage for 400k records + 2M invoice lines
Design/component library asset licensing (icon sets, theming tools)
Contingency buffer for third-party API/service costs (webhooks, email for password reset)

scenarios.name: P50 - Base estimate (labour + non-labour as scoped)
P70 - With 12% contingency for integration/migration unknowns
P90 - With 25% contingency (no historical actuals, thin DevOps capacity, migration risk)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project or team; estimate is derived purely from story points, task descriptions, and rate card.
Story points converted to engineering hours using a rough baseline of ~5-8 hours/point depending on task complexity and role mix.
Assumed project delivery window of approximately 14 weeks to sanity-check role hours against FTE capacity.

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) is thinly staffed relative to the critical-path CI/staging task (PW-1); this could bottleneck project start even though total hours fit within capacity over the full timeline.
QA effort estimated at roughly 15-20% of combined dev hours per task, scaled up for Urgent/High priority items.

Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumed to require significant Backend Developer effort for ETL scripting plus modest DevOps support for environment/cutover; no dedicated data engineer role exists on this team so Backend Developer absorbs this work.
Non-labour costs are rough allowances for third-party services (Stripe, cloud hosting, migration tooling) and may vary based on actual vendor contracts.
Priority breakdown totals reflect labour cost only, allocated per task priority; non-labour costs are not split by priority.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) has notable slack capacity, suggesting some tasks could be accelerated or the role could take on additional scope if needed.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal set (buttons, forms, tables only; defer theming tokens and dialogs) given it is Medium priority
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours on PW-2 from 90h to ~50h

reductions.description: Defer PW-6 (Invoice list and detail view) to a later phase since it is Medium priority and not required for initial launch
reductions.effect: Removes PW-6 entirely from this phase (Backend 30h, Frontend 40h, QA 12h)

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on lower-risk tasks (PW-2, PW-5, PW-6) by tightening test scope to critical paths only, relying more on automated regression from PW-1 pipeline
reductions.effect: Cuts ~28 QA hours across Medium/High priority non-payment tasks

reductions.description: Use a managed/off-the-shelf migration tool instead of custom scripting for PW-8, reducing Backend Developer hours needed for ETL work
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend Developer hours on PW-8 from 160h to ~110h

reductions.description: Delay non-critical non-labour spend (design/component library licensing) until PW-2 scope is confirmed post-descope
reductions.effect: Removes design/component licensing line item from this phase's budget
